historical_question: When, where, and for which referents do documentary acts use Dacia or competing regional names?
coverage_scope: Royal, ecclesiastical, and private charters concerning the medieval Kingdom of Hungary and Transylvania; sampling must be defined by date, issuer, and repository series before any absence can be evaluated.
survival_limitations: Survival and digitisation are uneven by issuer, archive, period, and series; the online catalogue is not a complete proxy for the surviving diplomatic corpus.
repository: National Archives of Hungary via Hungaricana
citation: Charter Database collection; calibration record DL-DF 12016, Acta Transsylvanica, 1428-10-08
notes: Catalogue and image access are verified; publication of Hungaricana digital material requires repository permission. No lexical search or witness review has been completed.

historical_question: How do narrative histories name Roman Dacia, the Danubian region, and the medieval polities treated as its successors?
coverage_scope: Latin narrative works with Romanian or Hungarian historical geography, beginning with Gesta Hungarorum and Thuróczy's Chronica Hungarorum; passages and recensions must be sampled explicitly.
survival_limitations: Late copies, editorial normalisation, variant recensions, and OCR or transcription quality can obscure wording; a searchable edition is not identical to a surviving witness.
repository: National Széchényi Library, Hungarian Electronic Library
citation: Gesta Hungarorum, MEK 19808; Johannes de Thurocz, Chronica Hungarorum (1488), MEK 10633
notes: Research access is verified. Textual passages must be checked against a named edition or witness, and image reuse needs a separate rights decision.

historical_question: Which curial administrative names are used for dioceses, rulers, and territories north of the Danube?
coverage_scope: Papal register series relevant to the Kingdom of Hungary, Transylvania, Wallachia, and Moldavia; register and folio ranges remain to be selected before querying names.
survival_limitations: The series is vast, selectively digitised, and mediated by calendars and editions; non-survival, non-digitisation, and non-selection are distinct from textual silence.
candidate_title: Registra Vaticana and related papal register series
repository: Vatican Apostolic Library / Vatican Apostolic Archive
citation: DigiVatLib manuscripts catalogue; exact register and folio range pending source-level selection
notes: A repository landing point, not a checked witness. BAV images permit study access but publication requires the repository's current authorisation process.

historical_question: Does a Black Sea commercial notarial corpus use Dacia, or instead port, polity, and route names, for its geographic frame?
coverage_scope: The 123 acts copied at Kilia by Antonio di Ponzo in 1360, used as a bounded calibration corpus for commercial naming rather than as a proxy for all Genoese notarial production.
survival_limitations: The surviving corpus is edition-mediated and represents one notary, place, and year; archival unit and act-level survival must be checked before any absence claim.
candidate_title: Actes de Kilia du notaire Antonio di Ponzo, 1360
repository: Archivio di Stato di Genova; edition distributed by De Gruyter Brill
citation: Michel Balard, Genes et l'Outre-Mer II (1980), acts pp. 23-194, DOI 10.1515/9783112319680
notes: The edition is a candidate text witness; no reproduction right is inferred from access, and exact archival act locators remain to be reconciled.

historical_question: What settlement and administrative names occur in Ottoman fiscal surveys, and can this source type answer the macro-regional lexical question at all?
coverage_scope: A bounded set of Ottoman tax registers for conquered Hungarian territories, with record-level place-name utility but no presumption that fiscal enumeration addresses the learned regional label Dacia.
survival_limitations: Only a subset is digitised; fiscal purpose, cataloguing level, language, and coverage vary. Surviving enumeration cannot be generalized beyond the register's stated fiscal scope.
candidate_title: Ottoman tax registers (defters) in the Hungarian National Archives
repository: National Archives of Hungary via Hungaricana
citation: Collection of Ottoman censuses; Tapu-Tahrir and related register descriptions, 1546-1619
notes: Not applicable to a claim that the learned macro-regional name is silent unless an individual register's purpose and scope make that question answerable. It remains applicable to settlement-name evidence.

historical_question: When does Dacia return as a learned regional label, and how is that label related to contemporary Hungary and Transylvania?
coverage_scope: Ortelius's 1570 Theatrum orbis terrarum, with the Hungary and Transylvania plates treated as a bounded late-sixteenth-century comparison rather than proof about medieval usage.
survival_limitations: One atlas state cannot establish a general date of return; plate states, language editions, and cataloguing or image sequence require verification.
repository: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
citation: Abraham Ortelius, 1570; G3200m.GCT00126; Hvngaria images 93-94 and Transsylvania images 95-96
notes: The Library of Congress reports this digitised collection as free to use and reuse unless an item advisory says otherwise. Plate readings are not yet transcribed or reviewed.
